data.short_description: Sal's Nashville Hot Chicken, a Dallas-Fort Worth-born chain, is planned for a new location at 9301 Southwest Freeway, Suite 270 in Houston's Braeburn neighborhood. Construction is expected to start this summer with a 2,100 sq ft build-out estimated at $240,000, wrapping up by year end. The brand is known for halal chicken sandwiches, tenders, and chicken & waffles.

data.status: permanently close after more than three decades
data.short_description: Ota-Ya, a Japanese restaurant in Newtown, PA, is preparing to permanently close after more than 31 years in business, with its final day of service on July 3, 2026, extended from an originally planned June 28 closure. Farewell dinner services are planned for July 1 through July 3. Owners Jeff Wong and Cindy are retiring to spend more time with family, and the property owners are reportedly planning to redevelop the site.

Fogo de Chão is set to open at Crabtree Valley Mall at 4325 Glenwood Avenue in Raleigh in late 2026, occupying the former Uncle Julio's 8,438-square-foot space. The Brazilian steakhouse chain offers a traditional churrasco dining experience with fire-roasted meats carved tableside. The Raleigh location is part of a broader North Carolina expansion that also includes planned locations in Durham and an August opening in Uptown Charlotte.

The team did not cite exact reasons in the closure announcement.

Mozzo is opening a fourth Charleston-area location after owner Shannon Campbell signed a lease, though the official address has not yet been revealed. Commenters have requested locations in Summerville, Daniel Island, West Ashley, and Clements Ferry. The new location joins existing Mozzo outposts on Coleman Boulevard, in Carolina Park in Mount Pleasant, and downtown on Meeting Street.

Habaneros, a Pan-Mexican restaurant concept from Louisiana, is opening its first Georgia location at Spring Quarter in Midtown Atlanta on the ground floor of Sora. The menu features Pan-Mexican cuisine inspired by flavors from Mexico and Latin America, including dishes such as Crawfish Nachos, Charred Grilled Octopus, and Short Rib al Carbon. The restaurant is designed with an Aztec-inspired aesthetic and offers handcrafted cocktails including its signature Chingona Margarita.

data.status: hopes to open Something Good in August
data.short_description: Something Good, a neighborhood bar concept, is planned for 4970 N. Lowell Blvd in Denver in the former Goldspot Brewing space, according to a city filing. Owner Greta Gunderson, who also runs Son of a Gun and Something Good in Kansas City, cited the space's exposed brick, patio, and garage door as key draws. The bar will feature draft beers, draft cocktails, yard beers, board games, and a TV.

Amoret, a new all-day café and cocktail bar from Kurt Henkel and Daniel Masters, is set to open this fall at 3100 Brighton Blvd in Denver's RiNo neighborhood. Masters, who also owns Hello Darling Cafe and Flora Cafe in Denver, described the concept as a gathering place from morning coffee through evening cocktails. The design is inspired by timeless European cafés, blending romantic textures, natural materials, and soft lighting.

The owners of HopScotch & Vine announced they would not be reopening at their downtown Plainfield location after 14 years in business. The owners posted a thank-you message to their community without specifying a final closing date.

The Mexican restaurant chain has been operating for more than 15 years with locations in Bolingbrook, Aurora, Romeoville, Lisle, St. Charles, and Oswego. No opening date has been announced.
